tasks.short: Develop and present technical proposals that meet customer requirements.

steps.what: Read customer documents and build a requirement matrix.

loop.input: Customer documents, including tables, attachments and submission instructions.
loop.output: Requirement matrix with source references, deadlines and unresolved ambiguities.
loop.check: Check attachment coverage, required fields and source references; engineer reviews omissions and ambiguity.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass; unreadable or ambiguous sections return to the engineer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Requirements appear in varied prose and tables; fixed parsing cannot reliably identify their meaning.

steps.what: Clarify priorities, constraints and acceptance criteria with the customer and account manager.
Check catalogue options, availability and costs in the {ERP}.
Confirm technical feasibility and resolve nonstandard commitments.
Write the proposal and requirement responses using approved technical material.

loop.input: Requirement matrix, approved design, calculated prices and approved answer library.
loop.output: Proposal draft with a cited response for each requirement and explicit gaps.
loop.check: Reconcile every requirement; validate prices deterministically; engineer verifies claims against cited sources.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass per section; unsupported claims remain gaps for the engineer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Customer-specific explanations need prose synthesis; templates still handle standard sections and numerical fields.

steps.what: Approve pricing, delivery promises and commercial exceptions.
Present the solution and discuss customer objections.
Send the approved version and record submission in the {CRM}.

tasks.design: A requirement-matrix generator reads customer files from the {DOCS}; deterministic rules combine catalogue and cost data from the {ERP} into a proposed configuration. A bounded drafting loop assembles cited answers, while approval routing in the {WORKFLOW} controls technical and commercial commitments. After presentation, changed commitments return for approval before the approved version is sent through the {EMAIL} and logged in the {CRM}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Product rules, past answers and pricing lived in separate places. Bespoke requirements still needed engineering judgement, making end-to-end automation unattractive.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of building document generators, validators and connectors. Bounded extraction and drafting can handle prose while established rules handle configuration and calculation.
tasks.still_hard: Maintaining product constraints, proving unusual performance claims and agreeing customer acceptance criteria remain expensive. Confidential customer files require controlled access under GDPR.
tasks.human_edge: Discovering the customer's real constraint and making a credible technical commitment when the standard catalogue is insufficient.

ambition.what: A requirement-by-requirement technical fit assessment before a full proposal.

tasks.altitude: The engineer spends less time assembling documents and more time testing solution assumptions with customers. Technical sign-off, pricing and contractual decision rights remain with their designated roles.

reach.task: Choose which technically uncertain opportunities deserve engineering capacity.
reach.learn: Opportunity qualification, capacity trade-offs and commercial risk.

evidence.claim: Tacton provides rule-based configuration and quoting; this supports the configuration component, not general proposal judgement.
The vendor's Meyn case reports substantially faster single-machine quoting after configuration rules were introduced.
Source-linked RFP drafting is feasible with a bounded loop, but completeness and technical accuracy require validation.
Time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates rather than measured outcomes.

assumptions: The baseline is a mixed catalogue and engineered-solution business, with the engineer coordinating specialist approval.
Build ranges cover one product family and a limited proposal format set.
Existing configuration features should be configured first when they cover the required rules.
Access estimates include GDPR review and employee consultation under national rules where applicable; they are not statutory timelines.
unknowns: How much of the product catalogue has explicit, maintained configuration rules.
Which technical claims and answers are approved for customer use.
Available interfaces, document quality, approval limits and actual proposal volumes.
Applicable employee-consultation requirements under national rules.
research_questions: Which extraction checks best detect requirements hidden in attachments and tables?
How accurately can source-coverage checks distinguish a supported answer from a merely related citation?
new_work: Review extracted requirements and unsupported answer gaps.
Maintain product constraints, approved answers and source expiry dates.
Handle connector failures and stale cost or availability data.
Revalidate changed proposals before external submission.

tasks.short: Work with the sales team to understand requirements and provide technical sales support.

steps.what: Review opportunity history and technical questions in the {CRM}.
Copy scattered account updates from the {EMAIL} and {CHAT} into opportunity notes.
Discuss requirements, buying concerns and technical uncertainties with the account manager.
Assemble relevant specifications, references and approved explanations from the {DOCS}.
Agree the sales approach, specialist involvement and next customer conversation.
Record agreed actions, owners and deadlines in the {CRM}.

tasks.design: Configure a shared opportunity view and a short action form in the {CRM}, so account updates are entered once and reminders follow agreed owners. A deterministic generator selects approved evidence from the {DOCS} using product and requirement tags, and flags unanswered questions. The engineer and account manager keep the discovery and sales-planning conversations.
tasks.previous_blocker: Useful context was spread across conversations and documents, with inconsistent opportunity records. Automating the conversation itself offered little value.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing record and reminder features can remove duplicate administration. AI-assisted coding makes a small evidence-pack generator practical without introducing an autonomous agent.
tasks.still_hard: Colleagues must keep the shared record useful. Ambiguous buying motives and disagreements about the sales approach still require direct discussion.
tasks.human_edge: Connecting technical uncertainty to the account manager's understanding of the buyer, politics and timing.

ambition.what: A scheduled technical qualification clinic for junior sales representatives.

tasks.altitude: The engineer spends less time reconstructing account history and more time coaching sales colleagues through technical qualification. Opportunity ownership and commercial approval rights do not change.

reach.task: Qualify technical fit before requesting a full demonstration or proposal.
reach.learn: Discovery questions, buying-process signals and when to escalate uncertainty.

evidence.claim: Shared opportunity records, filtered document retrieval and owner-based reminders can use configuration and deterministic code.
The supplied digest identifies advising and selling as human work; it supplies no direct case for replacing this collaboration.
Time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates rather than measured outcomes.

assumptions: The team uses a shared opportunity record but also copies updates from messages.
Approved material can be tagged by product, requirement and version.
Action owners enter agreed fields once; free-form meeting transcription is outside the initial scope.
Access ranges include GDPR review and employee consultation under national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Whether duplicate message-to-record copying is material in this team.
Existing shared views, action forms and reminder capabilities.
Quality of evidence tags and willingness to maintain shared records.
Applicable access restrictions and employee-consultation requirements under national rules.
research_questions: Which minimal discovery fields improve technical handovers without burdening sales representatives?
When does exact tagged retrieval stop being adequate for technical support questions?
new_work: Maintain evidence tags and retire obsolete material.
Review adoption and remove unused fields or reminders.
Maintain access permissions and failed reminder queues.

tasks.short: Prepare sales and service contracts with accurate technical schedules and approved terms.

steps.what: Reconcile customer details, scope and approved deal terms in the {CRM} and {ERP}.
Fill the contract template and attach the technical and service schedules.
Review customer redlines and identify departures from approved clauses.

loop.input: Deterministic document differences, customer additions and the approved clause playbook.
loop.output: Changed-clause list with playbook references, suggested categories and explicit uncertainties.
loop.check: Every changed span must appear; legal adviser verifies categories and reviews uncategorised text.
loop.stop: One classification and one correction pass; unmatched or ambiguous changes go to the legal adviser.
loop.why_not_simpler: Document comparison finds edits, but paraphrased obligations require contextual interpretation.

steps.what: Negotiate scope, liability and service obligations with the customer.
Approve the final contract and any exceptions within delegated limits.
Send the approved contract through the {ESIGN} for customer and authorised signatory signatures.
File the signed contract and hand its delivery obligations to the order clerk.

tasks.design: Validate approved deal fields from the {CRM} and {ERP}, then configure templates in the {DOCS} or existing {CLM} to assemble contracts and technical schedules. Deterministic comparison identifies all edits, and a bounded loop prepares a clause-exception list for legal review. Approval routing releases a specific version to the {ESIGN}; signature completion triggers filing and a structured delivery handover.
tasks.previous_blocker: Templates and deal fields were disconnected, and exceptions looked similar to standard drafting. Concern about binding errors discouraged automating even straightforward assembly.
tasks.enabler_now: Template assembly, field validation and signature routing are established capabilities. AI-assisted coding makes the connecting work cheaper, while bounded classification can prepare redlines for human judgement.
tasks.still_hard: Bespoke liability, acceptance criteria and cross-border service obligations require legal and engineering judgement. Poor deal data can produce a polished but incorrect contract.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding which obligations the business can accept and expressing technical boundaries that both parties understand.

ambition.what: A contract-to-delivery briefing for order clerks covering acceptance tests and service boundaries.

tasks.altitude: The engineer spends less time copying terms and more time checking delivery obligations before signature. Legal approval and signing rights remain with authorised roles.

reach.task: Translate signed scope and milestones into an accurate order handover.
reach.learn: Order acceptance, billing triggers, delivery dependencies and amendment controls.

evidence.claim: Realworks generates real-estate purchase agreements from CRM data; this is an assembly analogue, not evidence for technical contract review.
Deterministic validation and template assembly can handle approved deal fields; bespoke legal obligations still need authorised judgement.
A bounded clause classifier needs complete document comparison and legal review before its suggestions affect terms.
Time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates rather than measured outcomes.

assumptions: The engineer assembles technical schedules; an internal or external legal adviser handles material legal departures.
An existing template or contract facility supports field merging; otherwise deterministic generation adds scope.
Signature completion is an external dependency; the system does not sign for either party.
Build ranges cover one contract family and include GDPR access review plus employee consultation under national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Which clauses, schedules and fallback terms are approved.
Who can approve each obligation and who can sign.
Existing template, comparison, signature and contract-record capabilities.
Frequency of customer paper, redlines and conflicting deal records.
Applicable national contract rules and employee-consultation requirements.
research_questions: Which document comparison methods reliably capture changes in schedules, tables and attachments?
How should obligation handovers preserve traceability when a contract is later amended?
new_work: Maintain templates, clause playbooks and approval limits.
Resolve missing or conflicting deal fields.
Review classification gaps and substantive redlines.
Handle signature failures, amendments and incomplete delivery handovers.

tasks.short: Visit prospective buyers to demonstrate products and explain pricing, availability and technical advantages.

steps.what: Agree visit timing, attendees and site arrangements through the {EMAIL}.
Check current prices and availability in the {ERP}.
Select current catalogues and approved demonstration material from the {DOCS}.
Prepare physical samples and travel to the buyer's site.
Demonstrate products, inspect the application and discuss fit, pricing and availability.
Record buyer requirements and promised follow-up in the {CRM}.

loop.input: The engineer's typed visit notes and explicitly agreed follow-up.
loop.output: Draft requirement changes and actions with owners, dates and supporting note references.
loop.check: Engineer verifies commitments; missing owners or dates remain blank; record validation checks required fields.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass; ambiguous commitments return to the engineer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text site observations need interpretation; a structured visit form should replace this loop where sufficient.

steps.what: Send agreed information and confirm next steps through the {EMAIL}.

tasks.design: Configure visit booking and follow-up templates around the {CRM}, {CALENDAR} and {EMAIL}. A deterministic generator combines current {ERP} price and availability data with approved {DOCS} material into a dated visit brief. After the human demonstration, a bounded loop turns typed notes into proposed record updates and actions for the engineer to approve.
tasks.previous_blocker: Most time is physical travel, demonstration and discussion. The smaller preparation and follow-up steps crossed systems and rarely justified a separate integration project.
tasks.enabler_now: Small connectors and template generators are cheaper to build with AI-assisted coding. A bounded note-extraction loop can reduce paperwork without requiring recorded customer conversations.
tasks.still_hard: Physical demonstrations, site-specific judgement and trust remain human. Availability can change after preparation, and unusual site arrangements still require coordination.
tasks.human_edge: Observing the customer's actual application, adapting the demonstration and recognising concerns that the buyer has not clearly expressed.

ambition.what: A post-visit technical application note for the buyer's operations team.

tasks.altitude: The engineer retains a week dominated by customer visits, with less preparation and follow-up administration. Pricing and technical commitment authority do not change.

reach.task: Prepare repeatable demonstrations that expose relevant product limits.
reach.learn: Demonstration design, audience observation and explaining technical trade-offs.

evidence.claim: Verint creates call summaries and writes them to CRM records; this supports the paperwork pattern, not physical demonstration automation.
The AXA Health vendor case documents reduced after-call handling time in a service desk; transfer to sales visits is unproven.
Dated information packs, appointment templates and structured follow-up can use deterministic technology.
Time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates rather than measured outcomes.

assumptions: Travel and onsite interaction account for most of this task; preparation savings do not remove the visit.
The baseline uses typed notes rather than audio recording.
The initial scope uses one catalogue feed and approved follow-up templates.
Access estimates include GDPR review and employee consultation under national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Actual travel, preparation and follow-up time.
Whether prices and availability can be retrieved with reliable timestamps.
Whether a structured visit form can replace free-text extraction.
Site restrictions, customer scheduling practices and access to demonstration samples.
Applicable employee-consultation requirements under national rules.
research_questions: Which visit-note fields preserve technical context with the least entry effort?
How should pricing snapshots display expiry and refresh requirements during disconnected site visits?
new_work: Check extracted commitments and incomplete action details.
Maintain demonstration packs, templates and product mappings.
Handle stale availability, failed bookings and failed record updates.
Review generated application notes before sharing them externally.

role.altitude: The sales engineer moves document assembly and record maintenance into connected tools, while retaining discovery, demonstrations and technical commitments. More time goes to application fit and delivery boundaries; new commercial or signing authority requires explicit delegation.
reach: Help sales managers allocate engineering capacity using technical uncertainty and opportunity value.
Coach sales representatives on technical qualification before full proposal work.
Help order clerks turn signed technical scope into delivery and acceptance milestones.
skills_to_grow: Express product constraints and pricing logic as testable rules.
Maintain source-linked technical answers and document templates.
Validate model drafts against requirements, approved evidence and numerical checks.
Conduct application discovery and explain technical trade-offs.
Understand contract obligations, GDPR access controls and applicable national consultation rules.
role.ambitious_version: Offer a technical fit service that gives buyers a requirement matrix, an explicit gap assessment and a delivery-boundary briefing before a major purchase commitment.
